title: Pipeline, batch, and parallel
description: Load authors and drafts with independent reads, then save an author and draft in one transaction.

steps.label: Pipeline
steps.title: Send both reads on one connection
steps.body:
A drafts screen needs two lists, its authors and their drafts. With Drizzle ORM **1.0.0-rc.6**, `db.pipeline()` sends both selects back-to-back on one connection without waiting for the first result. Each query runs in its own transaction.

Press **Run**. Each result has a `status` and either a `value` or a `reason`. The results follow the input order.

meta.summary: Two result sets from queries sent on the same connection.

steps.label: Batch
steps.title: Save the author and draft together
steps.body:
Grace is a new author. We already know her ID, so we can build both inserts before sending them. `db.batch()` sends them in order inside one transaction. The post can reference the author inserted by the first statement.

Press **Run** to see both rows from `.returning()`. If you need to read a generated ID in JavaScript before building the second query, use an interactive `db.transaction()` for that flow.

meta.summary: One transaction inserts both rows and returns both results.

steps.label: Rollback
steps.title: Check what happens when the second insert fails
steps.body:
This time the new draft tries to reuse ID 1. PostgreSQL rejects it. The batch throws, and the transaction rolls back Grace's insert too.

Press **Run**. The follow-up select shows only Ada, even though Grace's insert was first in the batch.

meta.summary: A duplicate draft ID rolls back both inserts.

steps.label: Parallel
steps.title: Let the pool run independent reads concurrently
steps.body:
The same two reads can also use `db.parallel()`. It uses available pooled connections, and returns one settled result per query in input order. Use it when the queries can run independently.

Press **Run** to see the same two lists. Drizzle Run uses local PGlite, which serializes engine work. On a PostgreSQL server, how much can run at once depends on the connections available to the pool.

meta.summary: The pool dispatches each independent query and reports its outcome.

steps.label: Partial failure
steps.title: Keep the result of the query that succeeds
steps.body:
Run the same two statements through `db.pipeline()` and `db.parallel()`. The first tries to insert a draft with ID 1 again. The second loads the drafts.

In both groups, the insert returns `{ status: 'rejected', reason }` and the select returns `{ status: 'fulfilled', value }`. The call resolves with both outcomes in input order. Check each `status` before reading its `value` or `reason`.

Each statement runs independently, so a successful write can still commit when another statement fails. Use `db.batch()` when all the writes need to succeed together.

meta.summary: Both methods report the failed insert and still return the drafts.
